statement: Obtain the expansion of $(1+x)^{1/2}(1-2x)^{1/3}$ up to and including the term in $x^{2}$.
solution: $(1+x)^{1/2}=1+\\tfrac12x-\\tfrac18x^{2}+O(x^{3})$. $(1-2x)^{1/3}=1+\\tfrac13(-2x)+\\tfrac{(1/3)(-2/3)}{2}(-2x)^{2}+O(x^{3})=1-\\tfrac23x-\\tfrac49x^{2}+O(x^{3})$. Multiplying and keeping terms up to $x^{2}$: $1+(\\tfrac12-\\tfrac23)x+\bigl((-\\tfrac18)\cdot1+\\tfrac12\\cdot(-\\tfrac23)+1\\cdot(-\\tfrac49)\bigr)x^{2}=1-\\tfrac16x+\bigl(-\\tfrac18-\\tfrac13-\\tfrac49\bigr)x^{2}=1-\\tfrac16x-\\tfrac{65}{72}x^{2}$.
hints: Multiply the two series and keep only up to x^2.
Be careful combining the three x^2 contributions.
